rationale: Interpreted the repaired live-cluster receipt and closed the constructor question's fixture limitation. Receipt ea93eea3cc08408ab3cd208ca9b1e5ca evaluated all five comparisons: the restarted follower did not finish NewRaft within the window (violated, witness index 1), while the same stores restarted without the feature returned (holds, index 3), stayed at the snapshot index (applied_at_snapshot holds, index 3), faced a replay demand larger than the capacity observed on that very node (replay_exceeds_channel holds, index 3), and the remaining two voters kept a quorum (holds, index 2). Because the state was produced by normal cluster operations, the earlier limitation that no live node produced the gap is resolved, and the stall fact gains this receipt as an execution.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore, NewRaft cannot return when the replay must hand more batches to fsmMutateCh than that channel's 128-slot buffer holds, because the only consumer of the channel is runFSM, which NewRaft starts after the replay returns; the number of batches is ceil(committed-but-unapplied entries / MaxAppendEntries), so 129 entries above the last applied index stall the constructor with MaxAppendEntries 1 and 8193 entries do so with the default 64. Entries that never reach the FSM commit path (LogNoop) are skipped by prepareLog and do not create batches.
knowledge.conditions: Construction of a node whose log store reports a commit index above its snapshot/applied index while the feature is enabled; observed with in-memory stores, first on a harness-supplied node and then on a live three-node cluster whose follower accumulated 250 committed entries above its snapshot.

interpretations.rationale: The declared predicate is that a follower restarted with the feature over more committed entries than the FSM mutation channel can hold still finishes NewRaft within the observation window; it is contradicted by the witness. Admission index 0 records the state reached by ordinary operations: cluster {A,B,C}, leader B, snapshot index 7, staged commit index 257, 250 entries to replay and the gap flag true. The feature-on restart at index 1 never returned within 5s, while the control restart at index 3 returned as a follower with last_applied 7, i.e. still at the snapshot index, and that same event reports the observed capacity 128 and replay_exceeds_channel true, so the demand exceeded the channel even though the control constructed. Cluster status at index 2 confirms the other two voters kept a leader throughout, so the stalled node is the only failure. Mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs replays committed entries through processLogs into fsmMutateCh (api.go 724-754, raft.go 1296-1363) before NewRaft starts the only consumer runFSM (api.go 600-640), and the channel holds 128 batches (api.go 560), so once the send blocks the constructor cannot proceed. Limits: the restart used MaxAppendEntries 1, which is legal configuration but not the default; the non-return is observed over a 5s window and its permanence rests on the source argument that no consumer exists before the constructor returns; stores are in-memory and the shutdown graceful; the stalled instance is abandoned rather than resumed, and no supervision or application timeout is modelled.
counterevidence: The control restart over the same stores returned and stayed at the snapshot index, so the accumulated gap and the stores alone do not explain the stall.
The control event shows the same node observing a 128-slot channel that the fixture's demand exceeded, which is why the control's construction is not evidence against the mechanism.
limitations: The restart used MaxAppendEntries 1 rather than the default 64, so the observed gap (250 entries) is smaller than the default-configuration requirement of 8193.
Non-return is observed over a 5s window; permanence rests on the source argument about the missing consumer.
In-memory stores and a graceful shutdown; the stalled constructor is abandoned and no supervision is modelled.

interpretations.rationale: Answer: yes. A node whose log store reports a commit index that requires more batches than the 128-slot fsmMutateCh buffer cannot finish NewRaft, because the replay runs before the only consumer of that channel is started, and this now holds for a node whose gap was produced by ordinary cluster operations rather than by the harness. Receipt 00386ad8ea534d91a0ef7506fabc9527 witnesses it on supplied stores at two scales (141 batches from 9000 entries at MaxAppendEntries 64, and 200 batches from only 200 entries at MaxAppendEntries 1) with feature-off controls returning, and receipt ea93eea3cc08408ab3cd208ca9b1e5ca witnesses it in a live cluster: a follower running with the feature is snapshotted at index 7, receives 250 further committed entries bringing its staged commit index to 257, is shut down while the other two voters keep a quorum, and then never finishes NewRaft when restarted with MaxAppendEntries 1, while the same stores restarted without the feature construct and stay at the snapshot index. The source basis is restoreFromCommittedLogs -> processLogs -> fsmMutateCh with runFSM started only after the constructor returns. Remaining limits: the live restart used MaxAppendEntries 1, so at the default 64 a gap of 8193 entries would be needed, which is just above the default SnapshotThreshold and therefore depends on snapshot delay or failure; non-return is observed over a bounded window with permanence argued from source; stores are in-memory, the shutdown graceful, and the stalled constructor is abandoned without supervision, so no recovery path after the stall is exhibited.
counterevidence: Feature-off controls over the identical stores construct normally in both the supplied-store and live receipts, so the gap and the stores alone do not explain the stall.
No-op entries never reach the FSM commit path and do not stall construction, which scopes the defect to command or barrier entries.
The live cluster kept a quorum without the stalled node, so the defect is a node-level startup failure rather than a cluster-wide outage at that size.
limitations: The live reproduction used MaxAppendEntries 1; at the default 64 the required gap is 8193 entries, just above the default SnapshotThreshold, so how often a feature-enabled node reaches that gap is not established.
Non-return is observed over a bounded window; permanence rests on the source argument that no consumer of the channel exists before the constructor returns.
In-memory stores and a graceful shutdown; the stalled constructor is abandoned rather than resumed and no supervision, timeout or restart policy is modelled.

interpretations.joint_history: Three receipts over one question and one mechanism. 2d92d633d32a4a7c9e204b7dc5c8828b is retained as an identity failure (construct events without local_id, no evaluated comparison). 00386ad8ea534d91a0ef7506fabc9527 witnesses the stall on harness-supplied stores at two scales with feature-off controls. ea93eea3cc08408ab3cd208ca9b1e5ca reaches the same stall in a live three-node cluster whose follower accumulated the gap through ordinary operations, and its control reuses the same stores without the feature. They are compatible because the stall condition is the same in each (replay entries above the snapshot divided by MaxAppendEntries exceeds the 128-slot channel) and each receipt's comparison outcomes are read from that receipt alone; the live receipt's fixture (snapshot 7, staged commit 257, 250 entries) matches the supplied receipts' structure rather than their exact indexes.
